claim: There is no 'inference-pool-discovery' plugin (no k8s discovery plugin at all) in llm-d/llm-d-router's plugin architecture as of the main branch on 2026-09-11; the default Kubernetes pod-discovery path is a plain controller-runtime PodReconciler, and the only pluggable EndpointDiscovery implementation shipped is file-discovery, which is used to bypass Kubernetes entirely (not to replace the built-in Pod watch with a k8s-flavored plugin).
stance_target: existence of a distinct 'inference-pool-discovery' k8s plugin.go that replaced pod-selector-based discovery
scope_conditions: llm-d/llm-d-router repository, main branch, as fetched 2026-09-11
quoted_support: By default the EPP discovers inference endpoints by watching a Kubernetes InferencePool object and the pods it selects. The discovery plugin interface replaces that mechanism with a pluggable alternative so the EPP can run in environments where Kubernetes is not available.

claim: The default Kubernetes Pod-discovery event filter admits a Pod create/update/delete/generic event into reconciliation only if the Pod's labels match the InferencePool's selector, via Datastore.PoolLabelsMatch(pod.GetLabels()).
stance_target: label-selector-match is a gating condition for Pod discovery

claim: The reconcile-time datastore admission gate for a Pod is the logical AND of two conditions: podutil.IsPodReady(pod) and Datastore.PoolLabelsMatch(pod.Labels); failing either causes deletion from the datastore, and no other Kubernetes-specific field is checked at this step.
stance_target: the only filters on candidate Pods beyond label-selector-match are the aggregate Ready condition (no PodIP/NodeName/Phase checks)

claim: IsPodReady (pkg/epp/util/pod/pod.go, confirmed via direct fetch of the repository) checks only pod.DeletionTimestamp.IsZero() and the aggregate corev1.PodReady condition status; it does not inspect pod.Status.PodIP, pod.Spec.NodeName, or pod.Status.Phase, meaning a virtual-kubelet-backed Pod object that matches the selector and reports Ready=True would not be excluded by this readiness check regardless of which kubelet or provider set that condition.
stance_target: virtual-kubelet Pods matching selector + Ready=True are not excluded by any node/scheduling field check
scope_conditions: pkg/epp/util/pod/pod.go, function IsPodReady; cross-checked against docs/discovery.md prose in the same repository

claim: Even after a Pod passes the label-selector and Ready-condition gates, the datastore layer (podUpdateOrAddIfNotExist / extractActivePorts) builds one EndpointMetadata per matching pool.TargetPort using pod.Status.PodIP verbatim as Address with no emptiness or format validation; an empty or invalid PodIP is not itself a rejection condition at this layer, it would simply propagate into a broken endpoint address.
stance_target: no explicit PodIP validity check exists in the Kubernetes discovery path
scope_conditions: pkg/epp/datastore/datastore.go, function podUpdateOrAddIfNotExist (cross-checked via direct repository fetch, not the assigned URL)
quoted_support:
Address:     pod.Status.PodIP,
				NodeAddress: pod.Status.HostIP,
				Port:        strconv.Itoa(port),
				MetricsHost: net.JoinHostPort(pod.Status.PodIP, strconv.Itoa(port)),
